provenance: Chapter mood and symbolic-motif lists transcribed from the original suite JSON. Tone sentences and item-to-shot assignments are editorial syntheses. Reference images are native Halfworld movement midpoints rendered from its code; typography may differ by local font.

worlds.title: OUT OF LIFE
worlds.tagline: the maze, the haze, the fall, the ember

movements.label: THE SEARCH
movements.line: What we've made, we don't want. What we've sold — to the world, to ourselves — doesn't exist. I look for a way out: through the hallways, within the drawers, and fire escapes.

movements.label: MORE HAZE
movements.line: The vape gathers, inside and out. My vision blurs. I move toward the window — and you only get further away. More haze.

movements.label: THE FALL
movements.line: It was the maze, constructed by a tainted love. You fall off the fire escape, into darkness — and the city streaks upward like it's leaving too.

movements.label: AS DARK AS BLACK
movements.line: I trip on my own words, falling out of life — and find where you go when you leave. The gap between us breathes, and never closes.

motifs.haze: seeds at the window, claims the room left-to-right, becomes the sky he falls through
motifs.the-gap: 24px between the falling bodies; it breathes +-3 and never closes
motifs.words: his own lines fall beside him as tumbling dashes
motifs.the-ember: the last light in the film is the vape; white speck on black

characters.POET: black t-shirt; seated reading, then crossing to the glass; falls head-down, arm reaching
characters.EX: back only, every frame; vape ember pulses; recedes in three stations before the fall

worlds.logline: A poet reads aloud to a lover's turned back; the vape haze claims the room, the lover falls off the fire escape, and the poet falls behind — out of life — until it gets as dark as black.
worlds.thesis: The way out he searches for (hallways, drawers, fire escapes) is the way down; leaving is not an exit but a direction.
worlds.tone: Close, dim and withholding; yearning becomes spatial distance.

worlds.title: FLASHING LIGHTS

movements.label: SILENT SCREAM
movements.line: It was the type of silent scream a trapped lover makes to escape: a pending marriage, a concussion, a set of walls caving inward.

movements.label: THE MIRROR
movements.line: An emergency call while tossing and turning — the silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight, to digest a truth.

movements.label: WE GO THROUGH
movements.line: A winless insomnia. An epiphany of a road winding down. My eyes dilate — and we go through.

movements.label: THE GHOST WAS SEVEN
movements.line: I was six, I recall, when the ghost of a dead and love-less seven-year-old appeared, and shared that my parents' marriage wouldn't last. A warm, heavy breeze in winter, where a child is left home alone.

movements.label: BLINDS UP
movements.line: Curtains pulled, and blinds up as far and as wise as possible — to see flashing lights, and the whispering screams of two souls on a road winding down.

movements.label: THROUGH THE WINDOW
movements.line: And no tears, and no fucks, and no love to give. The ghost hands me a tambourine — and I throw it through the window.

motifs.light: the only ink: sweeps, cones, glow, cracks — the dark is the paper
motifs.the-pupil: dilation as door; the film passes through an eye to reach the past
motifs.the-road: winds down inside the window and inside the phrase
motifs.the-tambourine: arrives as a ring of light; exits toward the moon, bound for the chapel of Film 03

characters.POET: adrift in thin light; then a six-year-old drawn only as a black cutout against the window
characters.EX: curled in distress, faceless, drifting up and away — unreachable
characters.GHOST CHILD: shade-2 glow, feet dissolving above the floor; flickers in, whispers, dissolves, returns, hugs
characters.PARENTS: two 2px heads behind a lit rear window; their screams drawn as zigzags of light

worlds.logline: Floating in black between caving walls, a poet's eyes dilate until the pupil swallows the frame — and inside is age six: a window, a winding road, arguing headlights, a ghost with a tambourine, and the first throw.
worlds.thesis: The silent scream and the silent call are the same instrument; the tambourine is the first time the poet answers noise with noise.
worlds.tone: Hard light against black; vulnerability alternates with sensory assault.

worlds.title: HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT
worlds.tagline: the storm takes everything that was ever called goods

movements.label: ODE TO FOREVER
movements.line: Ode to forever — a tambourine sounds off an empty temple, empty choir stands, empty prayer lines.

movements.label: STILL WHOLE
movements.line: And abandoned baptism pools. It flies in through the rose window — still whole.

movements.label: COBWEBS
movements.line: Pews taken by cobwebs, and doused in disintegration. Spirits have left salvations in opened gift boxes, placed outside the side doors.

movements.label: UNTIL NOTHING REMAINS
movements.line: It thunders. Then rains until nothing remains. What was once love, now goods — broken and sealed apart by lightning. Daily breads, soaked and delivered rotted by rain; and blankets, soiled by venomous puppeteers.

movements.label: TWO SETS OF FOOTSTEPS
movements.line: Ode to the storm ending. Ode to two sets of mud-imprinted footsteps, leading away from what the water kept.

movements.label: SHATTERED
movements.line: And a tambourine, shattered into pieces. What if I followed this trail, to where the broken pieces have washed ashore?

motifs.the-inverted-frame: every thunderclap is one frame of the opposite register — the storm rehearses the ending
motifs.the-inventory: empty choir stands, abandoned baptism pool, opened gift boxes at the side door — the poem's own list, drawn
motifs.the-footsteps: two tracks writing themselves toward the water while nobody walks
motifs.the-flip: dawn arrives as a change of paper, not a change of light

characters.THE TAMBOURINE: the only actor: ring of light in the dark register, ring of ink in the white; one jangle per rotation; eight jingles at the end
characters.THE CHAPEL: a damage schedule: cross 0.25, spire 0.45, roof 0.55-0.7, walls 0.8; rubble accumulates at the base

worlds.logline: The tambourine thrown at age six flies into a chapel still whole, waits at the altar step through the cobwebs, and a time-lapse storm takes the building down to two stubs and a doorway — then the storm ends, the film turns white, and the tambourine falls one last time and shatters among two sets of footprints.
worlds.thesis: An engagement is broken the way a chapel decays: first the cross tilts, then the roof, then the register of the world itself — and the gift that started it all only breaks after everything it was thrown at is gone.
worlds.tone: Abandoned ceremonial space; decay gives way to a pale, emptied shore.

worlds.title: NEVERMORE
worlds.tagline: a trail followed twice, a vow made twice

movements.label: WASHED ASHORE
movements.line: What if I followed this trail, to where the broken pieces have washed ashore — and the ashes of expired wildfires cover sands, and debris lifted from the night sea water’s floor.

movements.label: FOLDED WHISPERS
movements.line: The waves calm to folded whispers; the winds mute the trees. The right level of silence, to find a throbbing heart — it used to be mine. I lift it with care: nevermore.

movements.label: MUSTARD SEEDS
movements.line: What if I followed this reclaimed heart, to where the puzzle pieces of faith are handcrafted — scrambled and scattered as mustard seeds into the vast moonlit night’s garden fields.

movements.label: THEY TURN TO FACE ME
movements.line: The plants in a golden hue bloom, and face toward me in anticipation. The weeds repel, falling into the shadows where our memories hide — and mean so little, in a moment of defeat — as I’m called forward.

movements.label: DEEPEST DARKNESS
movements.line: The clouds mute the stars for the deepest level of darkness — welcoming extra hard work, to search the bare ground for two hands.

movements.label: I PUT THEM BACK ON
movements.line: Hands that once could touch dust after dusk, and feel good — they too used to be mine. I put them back on, with the care of my future at stake: nevermore.

symbols: Throbbing heart/Familiar heart/Reclaimed heart/Dusk settled heart
Moonlit night’s garden fields/Golden hue plants

motifs.the-register-descent: dusk as formal device: the film darkens in steps and crosses to black mid-beat
motifs.no-arms: the figure system withholds arms for five beats; their return IS the climax
motifs.golden-heads: shade 0-1 plant heads leaning toward his x every frame — anticipation drawn literally
motifs.false-glints: the ground lies twice before it tells the truth

characters.POET: two-tone red/black torso, sunglasses brow-bar, chest hole until the heart reseats; no arms drawn until beat 6
characters.THE HEART: a 3px pulse that travels home in a shallow arc
characters.THE HANDS: two glowing mitts with finger ticks; the only shade-0 objects on the ground
characters.RAVENS: three flying over the shore; two perched to wait out the search

worlds.logline: In red and black, hands in pockets, a poet walks the shore of everything that broke, lets a heart lift itself back into his chest, follows the trail into a night that falls through the film's own register, and searches a bare field until his hands — they too used to be his — return, and the arms are drawn for the first time.
worlds.thesis: Recovery is not retrieval: the heart and the hands come back on their own terms, and the self's only work is to walk, kneel, and receive — nevermore said once per organ.
worlds.tone: Patient and solitary; small false glints delay the bodily restoration.

worlds.title: BLOODLINES
worlds.tagline: he names the stars after the people who made him

movements.label: NAME MY OWN STARS
movements.line: Now go, they tell me. To ask if I can inherit the earth — to ask if I can name my own stars. Even galaxies, if I may.

movements.label: SOUTHERN PINE
movements.line: The past, too, was waiting for me — coming of age in the shared rooms of humid basements as bedrooms; mattress pads where the wood beams of Southern pine could comfort my spine. It didn’t. To dream was to prevail.

movements.label: A NEW UNIVERSE
movements.line: They tell me: ask if I can invent a new universe — if God would let me, little ole me, award a blessing here and there. Even grant miracles.

movements.label: BEWARE OF ME
movements.line: In uncertain times, in forsaken times. Their blood flows through my hands — fingerprints that orchestra great powers — sun-kissing my skin, deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries. Beware of me.

movements.label: THE GATES OPEN
movements.line: The gates open with wings — gifted from evolution, and made of marble stones kissed by the hymns our Creator composed, with an orchestra of our ancestors’ wildest dreams, to welcome us.

symbols: Deepening voice/Baritone of a million cries/Unanswered plight

motifs.gifts-descending: star (2px) to galaxy (spiral) to universe (twin spirals) — scale as blessing
motifs.the-white-window: memory as the only white surface in a black film
motifs.it-didnt: the middle beam sags twice, on cue with the line
motifs.the-inversion: entering the light costs the figure its light

characters.POET: carved light, two-tone, arms and hands in use for the first full film; goes dark silhouette inside the gate seam
characters.ANCESTORS: crowned A-robes, shade 2 with shade-0 crowns; three offer stars, two flank the gates with arms up
characters.THE GALAXY: a two-arm spiral on the ORBIT lookup; its invented twin counter-rotates
characters.THE BASEMENT: a white window in the night: three pine beams, a mattress pad, a slit of light, humidity on the walls

worlds.logline: Told NOW GO, the poet walks into a parade of crowned ancestors who hand him stars to name, lower a galaxy into his returned hands, hover his basement childhood in the sky as a white lit room, run their blood through his fingerprint whorls until his voice drops to a baritone of a million cries — and open marble gates with wings to welcome him through.
worlds.thesis: Inheritance is not received but conducted: the blood is an orchestra, the stars take new names, and the gates only open for a body that has already gotten its heart and hands back.
worlds.tone: Solemn inheritance with growing defiance; scale expands from body to cosmos.

worlds.title: RESURRECTING ATLANTIS
worlds.tagline: a city comes up out of the water

movements.label: THE COMETS
movements.line: Poets, who eased generations down yellow brick roads — and plucked our souls out of their secret places, to follow comets to the capital city of our collective consciousness.

movements.label: THE WATERLINE FALLS
movements.line: Resurrecting Atlantis. Here we are all one — the pact we've made here with nature, abandoned and hoped for the best, back on life.

movements.label: ADMISSION
movements.line: A relearned currency, we reassess as the admission. But here we are all safe. An unfamiliar, flickering candle light, illuminating smiles at night.

movements.label: NARROW STREETS
movements.line: Where shadows cast from narrow streets beaming with love — in the joyful noises that color rainbows, and give us infinite time to heal, and set clouds free.

movements.label: CROSSHAIRS TO CONTINUUMS
movements.line: I know my soul — and it could stay here forever. Leaving behind crosshairs for continuums, and strains for serendipity.

movements.label: WELCOMING ALL
movements.line: A city born in unison, out of the purest of fictions — welcoming me, and welcoming all.

motifs.currency: the star handed down in Film 05 spent here — inheritance become admission
motifs.the-drain: resurrection as subtraction: nothing rises, the covering falls
motifs.rainbow-noise: sound drawn as geometry: burst, then three bands
motifs.pulse-sync: belonging rendered as phase-lock between chest and windows

characters.POET: carved light with two orbiting stars after the admission (three before); goes shade-7 in the door glow
characters.THE CANDLE: unsure of itself until it is paid; then a star
characters.THE CITY: seven towers with a full submerged height, revealed by the drain; windows in blue-and-pink alternation (shades 1/3)
characters.THE QUEUE: three guests who cross the same glow and go dark the same way

worlds.logline: Down a road that lights its own bricks, past comets all pointing one way, the poet watches a drowned city let go of its water, pays the gate with one of his named stars, wanders streets where every joyful noise blooms a rainbow, stands in a plaza until the whole city blinks with his heart — and follows the music into a house.
worlds.thesis: A city born in unison out of the purest of fictions is entered the way faith is: you pay with something you were just given a name for, and the light at the door costs you your own.
worlds.tone: Expansive, serene and welcoming; belonging is expressed through shared rhythms.

worlds.title: DJ TURN ME UP

movements.label: CHIN NESTED
movements.line: DJ, turn me up, please. Eyes wide shut, chin nested at the arch of the weight of these spoken words.

movements.label: VINEYARD GHOSTS
movements.line: I have a love story to tell — of ghosts, whispering unfolded dilutions, birthed in purity, and dying in the vineyards of sun-soaked evergreen fields, unnourished.

movements.label: THOUSAND LIGHT YEARS
movements.line: One by one, treasures escaping — devaluing themselves after unsullied stars diminished their glares. I walked a thousand light years to be heard. So DJ — please — turn me up.

movements.label: DIVERGING RINGS
movements.line: So I can speak: of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a shared home, boxed and trucked on separate one-way streets — not built with U-turns, or stop, maybe-we-shouldn't signs.

movements.label: ELEVEN PETALS
movements.line: A love story of years — eleven years — each plunkled off as daisy petals. We love, we not. Of a future gone swiftly, and a past left empty-handed.

movements.label: THREE ROADS
movements.line: To pick a road: of heavy rain. Or of frontal fog. Or of dimmed night lights under a cloud — with a silver lining.

movements.label: CHIN HIGH
movements.line: Now, turning forth to face delights and shadows — one night at a time; one tear at a time; one open mic at a time. Chin now nested high, and volume turnt up.

motifs.volume-as-form: the film's density is its loudness
motifs.projections: memory as outline panels in air — distinct from Film 05's white-filled window
motifs.we-love-we-not: alternating with each detachment; year eleven lands on LOVE
motifs.the-silver-lining: one shade-0 line under a dim cloud, the only edge lit

characters.POET: at the mic, chin down then high; the brow-bar carries eyes-wide-shut; two orbit stars remain
characters.THE DJ: dropped in on a light beam; drawn scratching, hands only
characters.THE FADER: the ninth character: present in every frame, level 1 to clipping
characters.THE DAISY: eleven petals on the PET11 table, plunked on a fixed schedule; the center holds

worlds.logline: A DJ is lowered into the house on a beam of light, the needle rings the room, and the poet — eyes wide shut, chin nested down — tells the whole love story over a rising fader: ghosts in vineyards, rings diverging, a home trucked apart, eleven petals plunked off a daisy, three roads and one silver lining — until the chin nests high and the volume clips.
worlds.thesis: Being heard is a gain structure: the same story at level one is grief and at level eight is testimony — the fader, not the words, is what turns forth to face delights and shadows.
worlds.tone: Exposed and insistent; the performance moves from lowered chin to claimed voice.

worlds.title: NEWLY SINGLE
worlds.tagline: a soul leaves a body on a dance floor

movements.label: PULSING
movements.line: Pulsing, and head throbbing from the music — and empty, on a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations.

movements.label: THE ESCAPE
movements.line: The soul escapes my body, and leaves him on the dance floor — just flesh and bones. Rejection and heartache hit different, with no feelings afloat.

movements.label: IMAGINE MY BODY
movements.line: I want my soul to imagine my body. Watch strangers collide and spark electric currents that gamut the mood. We want him to be the last to leave.

movements.label: THE EQUATOR
movements.line: Now let us put my soul in the middle of an open field — at the equator of a planet much larger than my own, and much hotter.

movements.label: COOL ME DOWN
movements.line: Cool me down: pouring unfiltered water out of ice baths, salted from the closest moons, from angles of the newest religions — their graces curse or bless me. Only infinity will tell.

movements.label: BACK TO MY BODY
movements.line: Now bring my soul back to my body: to lean back, breathe in the smoke that fills the room — how good it is to finally get acquainted with the night.

movements.label: MOUNTAINS IN THE DISTANCE
movements.line: Unfamiliar, yet relatable mountains in the distance; wandering thoughts within reach. Accepting you'll never say, nor feel, my love was real. What isn't mine, I still can not give.

motifs.two-clocks: the film's grammar: jitter vs. glide in the same frame
motifs.the-haze-grown-up: Film 01's vape returns as the smoke he chooses to breathe
motifs.the-withheld-ring: the suite's first gesture refused on purpose

characters.POET-BODY: two-tone until the split; then a single-shade husk on the fast clock, no bar, no pulse
characters.POET-SOUL: a thin outline of light on the slow clock, carrying both named stars
characters.ANGELS: two winged pourers on the slow clock, vessels tilted, streams converging on the husk
characters.THE RING: six segments; trembles on every fourth frame; never crosses the railing

worlds.logline: On a rooftop running faster than its own night, the poet's soul steps out of his body, watches all of Atlantis top-down, stands at the equator of a hotter planet, lets angels pour moon-salted ice baths over the husk he left dancing — then returns, leans back, breathes the whole room in, and at the railing holds a ring out over the edge and cannot let it go.
worlds.thesis: Separation is a frame-rate: the body grieves at the world's speed and the soul at its own — and what returns from the split is not relief but accuracy: what isn't mine, I still can not give.
worlds.tone: Restless bodily rhythm against the slower drift of the soul.

worlds.title: YET, HEARD

movements.label: THE SHARED MOON
movements.line: Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it. We talk for years, travel through time — we grow old together, I believe. Maybe we could have it all.

movements.label: TEARS, AN ABYSS
movements.line: Before I go, I call on my mother — in tears, speaking of an abyss she's never known. We talk for years, re-closet wounds, and re-explain my way of birth. Even after prayer: what isn't mine, I still can not give.

movements.label: HIS FOOTSTEPS, RETRACED
movements.line: Before I go, I call on my father — his calming demeanor summoned from the yonders. We walk for years, east toward the sunrises, retracing his footsteps — my tears falling in the wave shadows of the inner harbor.

movements.label: EAST, AT THE HARBOR
movements.line: We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken. Someone borrowed, and someone blue — yet, broken. Yet, heard.

motifs.time-compression: moon phases, tree seasons, window generations around one steady walk
motifs.the-inset: the living room as a panel whose border collects the tears
motifs.the-borrowed-suitcase: what stays standing after the person is weather

characters.EX: back-turned in every appearance, as always; dissolves stroke by stroke, leaving a suitcase
characters.MOTHER: seated in an inset living room with a lamp and a prayer above her head
characters.FATHER: walks a half-step ahead; his footprints light when the son's feet find them
characters.THE PAIR: the background clock: gap 2 to 24 pixels across four beats

worlds.logline: Through a fawning crowd, past a moon that runs its phases over one walk, into a phone booth twice — mother's living room arriving as an inset with a tear down its crease, father's footprints lighting under his son's feet — while the break-up widens in the background of every shot, until the EX dissolves to weather and a motorcycle blinks its lamp at the man left standing.
worlds.thesis: Farewell is not an event but a background process: it runs at its own rate behind every call, every walk, every prayer — and being heard does not stop it; it only means someone watched it happen with you.
worlds.tone: Tender but unresolved; adjacent spaces hold grief without settling it.

worlds.title: MAGIC RIDE
worlds.tagline: night replaced by morning, dot by dot

movements.label: HOP ON
movements.line: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are — blissful, and oddly sensitive. I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings, and hop on.

movements.label: HEADS TWIST
movements.line: Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell — being everywhere, with no one to love. I let the noise block the noise. The way I ride: eyes turn, heads twist — and prove the magic still exists.

movements.label: MOON SETTLES
movements.line: All preparations to live and dream in darkness, I no longer desire. The moon settles, and the tease of distant stars subsides — and I can see a morning ahead for me.

movements.label: NIGHT REPLACED
movements.line: It looks like a morning I could believe in — a morning where loss and life aren't so — well — ripe with sunlight that's deceptively warm. The chirping of birds, fueling of nests, spring out of the night that has covered me.

movements.label: BLISSFUL, INNOCENT
movements.line: With my own curiosities, for a chance at an end wherever everything will be OK. I want to live in this feeling forever — blissful, and oddly innocent.

movements.label: CHILLY MORNING
movements.line: Riding in a way you can't help but double-click — and prove the magic still exists. Even here, it's chilly in the morning.

motifs.the-crossing: register as landscape: crossed, not flipped
motifs.stars-come-inside: the orbit radius decays to zero; the pulse doubles
motifs.the-borrowed-suitcase: strapped behind the seat all the way to the shore
motifs.the-breath: the only cold thing in a warm frame — 'even here'

characters.POET: rider profile, leaning forward; brow-bar; heart pulse 1px in the dark, 2px after the stars come inside
characters.THE MACHINE: hex wheels with rotating spokes, tank, lamp; blissful and oddly sensitive; carries the borrowed suitcase
characters.THE BYSTANDERS: three, each with a two-tick head twist and a doubleclick blink
characters.LONELINESS: an eight-blob weather system, shredded on contact with the noise

worlds.logline: Not looking for a ride, he rubs his aggressions into the steel anyway — and one ride carries the whole film from black to white: through streets where heads twist twice, past loneliness shredded by his own noise, under a settling moon, across a grey hour where the frames themselves trade registers, into a believable morning that is chilly, and back to the shore where everything broke — arriving this time, not washing up.
worlds.thesis: The magic still existing is not an event but a direction: darkness is crossed at riding speed, the stars you were given come inside, and the same shore means something different when you choose to stop there.
worlds.tone: Independent, quietly amused and increasingly open; night gives way to morning.

worlds.title: NEW DAY
worlds.tagline: the temple assembles, one course at a time

movements.label: MORNING FOG
movements.line: Fog covers the seas and hugs the tree-covered hills, floating through the morning as it exhales its introduction. This world is at peace.

movements.label: FIRST COURSES
movements.line: In the awakening of dawn, in fresh muted colors: we can rebuild this temple. It's a new day — a catharsis for me to say, with newfound energies and recycled airs.

movements.label: COLUMNS AND BEAMS
movements.line: We can rebuild this temple — under vibrant sun rays of glory, of the wisdoms of morning dews and their winks of luck.

movements.label: THE INFINITY POOL
movements.line: With laps around infinity pools of edgeless dreams, that reflect the enormity of the skies.

movements.label: WALKING ON WATER
movements.line: And of modern faiths — that we too can walk on water. Deep breaths, in appreciation of present life, and our present positions.

movements.label: A NEW DAY
movements.line: We can rebuild this temple. It's a new day. A catharsis. We can welcome a new day.

motifs.walking-on-water: faith as a compositing trick the film commits to

characters.THE TEMPLE: an assembly parameter: platform 0.05, pillars 0.26, shell 0.34-0.62, inner sweep, needle 0.72, ramp 0.78, opening 0.85, fins 0.92

characters.THE REFLECTION: the same function, mirrored about y=66, shades folded to 1-2, wobbling with the water

worlds.logline: The fog exhales its introduction over the ruin, and the ruin answers by lifting itself: stones float into a new base course, the broken arch straightens into a doorway, a parabolic shell draws itself left to right — and when the water arrives edgeless, the temple learns to reflect, the poet walks the waterline with his own inversion underfoot, and the sun ends up overhead.
worlds.thesis: Catharsis is construction with the original materials: nothing new arrives — the same stones, the same arch, the same man — only the schedule runs the other way.
worlds.tone: Calm reconstruction; masonry answers the earlier chapel damage.

worlds.title: REUNION
worlds.tagline: less time for words, more space for laughter

movements.label: HUGS WITH NO REASON
movements.line: Decades later, there is less time for words, and more space for laughter — hugs with no reason, and loud voices, so our hearts can be overheard.

movements.label: LESS TIME, MORE SPACE
movements.line: Less time for words. More space for laughter.

movements.label: ELDERS, NOW PAST
movements.line: Reflecting on legacies, and creeds once told — of elders, now past.

movements.label: BURNING HOURGLASSES
movements.line: And is this a one-time occasion? we ask. Or will we make time, in the sands of burning hourglasses?

movements.label: WINDS PART
movements.line: Before our winds part ways — to a next lifetime. This is brotherhood.

motifs.the-flip: the poem's question answered by a hand, not a line

characters.THE HOURGLASS: burning grains with one-pixel flames; flipped at 0.55-0.68 of its beat

worlds.logline: Decades later, inside the temple they rebuilt, three friends arrive through a door of light, trade their words in for laughter, go quiet for the crowned elders who stand faintly among them, flip the burning hourglass rather than let the occasion be one-time — and part ways trailing curls of wind, hearts still blinking in unison.
worlds.thesis: Brotherhood is a shared clock: the hug synchronizes it, the laughter funds it, the flip extends it — and the winds can part ways without breaking the tempo.
worlds.tone: Warm familiarity; individual gestures become shared laughter.

worlds.title: HOW TO WIN MY HEART

movements.label: SMALL TABLES
movements.line: Find me at the harbor, at the small tables, watching.

movements.label: COUNTED ORBITS
movements.line: The couples orbit each other the way Jupiter keeps its moons — close, and counted.

movements.label: BURNED STORIES
movements.line: The elders clutch their pearls and pray. Life has burned all my love stories — victory-less seasons.

movements.label: HARVESTED POWER
movements.line: So I harvest the flowers instead — scarlet poppies, purple blossoms — and they become my power.

movements.label: REFOCUS
movements.line: Then, a distant window. She says: you'll see me. Capture the eyes. Refocus. Step back. Say hello.

movements.label: WON'T LEAVE
movements.line: Don't make me leave. I escaped here for a reason.

motifs.orbital-watching: desire studied as mechanics before it is risked
motifs.char-eaten-pages: the burned stories kept, not discarded
motifs.the-focus-pull: attention drawn as rendering: two frames where only she is solid
motifs.the-staying: the suite's second refusal (after the withheld ring) — this one toward, not away

characters.POET: seated more than standing, for the first time in the suite; bouquet of eight; bold outline once the power is worn
characters.HOPE: a silhouette in one lit window across the water, facing out; never closer than distant
characters.THE ELDERS: two benches — one pair clutching pearls, one praying
characters.THE FLOWERS: poppies as dark rounds, blossoms as crossed dots; ten stalks, eight taken

worlds.logline: At the harbor cafe he watches couples orbit like Jupiter's moons and elders clutch what they kept, while his own love stories sit char-eaten at his elbow — so he harvests the flowers into his power instead, until a distant lit window says YOU'LL SEE ME, and instead of leaving toward anything, he sets the bouquet on the rail and sits back down: don't make me leave; I escaped here for a reason.
worlds.thesis: Winning this heart is not pursuit but placement: stay where you escaped to, put the gathered power somewhere visible, and let the window keep its light on.
worlds.tone: Watchful and guarded; attention gradually risks remaining with another person.

worlds.title: HOT MINUTE
worlds.tagline: everything learns to be weather, then a door

movements.label: EVERYTHING I BUILT
movements.line: A hot minute. The haze gathers on the water — and everything I built here learns to be weather: the city, the temple, the harbor.

movements.label: FROM THE GROUND UP
movements.line: It takes me last, and from the ground up. I am reluctant — but I have been weather before.

movements.label: NO WALLS
movements.line: All black again. But no walls this time.

movements.label: THE REEL
movements.line: A life flashes the way a reel does: the window, the tambourine, the field, the stars, the candle, the daisy, the ride, the temple, the hourglass.

movements.label: TWO ENTWINED MUSES
movements.line: Our dance together is a victory — two entwined muses, as it ends.

movements.label: I CHOOSE THE DOOR
movements.line: An old door, from a vintage somewhere. It opens on a slow party — the kind I once fell out of a window to escape. This time, I choose the door.

motifs.fade-schedules: each built thing greys on its own clock; the flowers hold longest
motifs.the-suite-recalled: twelve memory panels: the films as their own B-roll

characters.POET: taken feet-first, pulse last; floats whole in the black; enters the door back-turned — the suite's final figure is himself, seen the way the EX always was
characters.THE HAZE: the suite's antagonist material completing its arc: vape, dissolution, smoke, weather, and finally the medium of passage
characters.THE MUSE: the thin light outline, entwined for one beat, never named
characters.THE DOOR: vintage, paneled, knob glinting; opens on warm silhouettes at half clock; closes to a line, then keeps what it took

worlds.logline: The haze gathers on the water and takes everything he built — boats, cafe, her window gently, the flowers last — then takes him ground-up until only the pulse blinks in the black. What follows is the suite remembering itself in twelve flashes, a dance of two entwined muses around one center, and an old vintage door opening on a slow warm party: the kind he once fell out of a window to escape, and now walks into, from the back, at his own speed, as the door closes and keeps him.
worlds.thesis: Leaving and arriving are the same door seen from different registers: the suite opens with a fall out of a window and closes with a walk through a door — and the victory is not escaping the party, but choosing it.
worlds.tone: Intense but accepting; built forms dissolve while remembered relations recur.
